findings.message: The insert now uses a bare `on conflict do nothing`, so it swallows every unique violation, not just the key and source_ref ones. In conflictOf, when the key lookup finds no row, `(taken?.key) ?? input.key` still reports "project key X is taken" with existingKey = input.key. A conflict it could not identify is reported as a known key clash. Fix: when neither lookup finds a row, throw an error that says the conflict is unidentified (existingKey null), or name the arbiters explicitly (`on conflict (tenant_id, key)` plus the source_ref partial index) so other constraints still fail loudly.
findings.scenario: A conflict on any other unique constraint of delivery.project (or a key row that RLS hides because the key's uniqueness spans tenants) → ProjectConflictError('project key K is taken', existingKey 'K'), but no project K is visible to the caller.

findings.message: The new sourceRef format only accepts lowercase letters in the module part (`^[a-z]+\.`). Several module ids in the architecture contain a hyphen: it-access, payroll-lk, payroll-au, inbox-agent. Any of these modules that calls the contract with its own reference fails validation. So the namespace rule only works for the presales example. Fix: derive the module part from the module-id rule (allow `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`), or validate it against the registered module ids. Add those ids to the variant table.
findings.scenario: createProject(ctx, { key: 'ITA', ..., sourceRef: 'it-access.request:R12' }) → ValidationError 'module.record:id', though the reference is well-formed for that module

findings.message: createProjectInTx has been removed from the published contract (it was published in T2), and the test label 'AC-3', which covered it, now covers conflict handling instead. The README was updated, but nothing in the diff updates the change's AC-3 in change.md or notes the contract removal for consumers. Fix: update change.md so that AC-3 matches, and record the removal in the README's contract notes in case presales already builds against it.

The duplicate-key fix lives in the shared insertProject, so it also changes the general createProjectService path (UI action, MCP create_project, chat confirm). Those paths now throw ProjectConflictError, a plain Error subclass, where they used to throw a raw unique violation. The previous finding asked for a clear conflict on both entry points. The new table only drives the contract `createProject`. No test drives a taken key through createProjectService or the MCP/chat callers, or shows how they surface the error to the user (tool error or validation message, not an internal error). Fix: extend the AC-3 table to run each conflict variant through createProjectService and registry.call('create_project'), and assert the error the caller actually sees.
findings.scenario: MCP create_project { key: 'CON', ... } where CON exists → ProjectConflictError thrown through the registry; untested whether it becomes a ToolError or a 500

findings.message: The fix limits sourceRef to the contract but does not tie its module part to the calling module. Any contract caller can still pre-claim another module's reference (e.g. presales.opportunity:OPP0042). If it uses the same key, presales then gets `existing: true` for a project it did not make. Consider checking the prefix against the caller's module identity.
findings.scenario: Module X calls createProject({ key: 'ABC', sourceRef: 'presales.opportunity:OPP0042' }); presales' Promote with the same key → { existing: true } for X's project

findings.message: ProjectConflictError carries its own `retryable = false` flag and conflict taxonomy next to core's ValidationError/ForbiddenError. If core already has a conflict error class, this is a second copy that callers and error mappers must learn to handle separately. Prefer core's conflict error, or add a ConflictError to core.

When a create finds the project this sourceRef already made, it still runs as a full defineService write. It appends a 'delivery.project.create' audit row against a project that was not created, and under withIdempotency it counts as a write. Audit readers will see two create records for one project. Consider a distinct audit action (or none) for the existing path.
findings.scenario: Promote retried after a lost response → two delivery.project.create audit rows for the same project id
